'Beware of Rabbi Akiva and his Torah,'" etc.;
וְכֵן מָצִינוּ שָׁם גַּבֵּי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
and so we find there regarding Rabbi Meir.
That is, had they, chas v'shalom,
לֹא הָיָה בְּכֹחָם לִכְבּוֹשׁ הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע;
they would not have had the strength to conquer the yetzer hara;
רַק עַל יְדֵי הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה שֶׁלָּהֶם
only through their words of Torah —
"Hashem will not abandon him into his hand" —
and they proclaimed about them in Heaven:
"Beware of Rabbi Akiva and his Torah,"
"Beware of Rabbi Meir and his Torah."
וְאָמַר שֶׁלֹּא רַק רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר וְכַדּוֹמֶה,
And it says that not only Rabbi Akiva, Rabbi Meir and their like,
which is the crown of the Torah,
זוֹכֶה אֲשֶׁר ה׳ לֹא יַעַזְבֶנּוּ בְיָדוֹ
merits that "Hashem will not abandon him into his hand,"
וּמוּבְטָח לוֹ שֶׁהוּא בֶּן עוֹלָם הַבָּא.
and is assured that he is a ben Olam HaBa.
that of himself he has no strength to prevail,
only with the help of Hashem Yisbarach, as stated.
And so it is expounded (Bava Basra 17a),
that the yetzer hara had no dominion over them
and the Angel of Death had no dominion over them.
So too, anyone who learns halachos,
זוֹכֶה שֶׁלֹּא יִשְׁלוֹט בּוֹ יֵצֶר הָרָע —
merits that the yetzer hara will not dominate him —
"Hashem will not abandon him into his hand" —
and that the Angel of Death will not dominate him.
Even though the entire blemish has not been rectified,
וְלֹא זָכוּ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה בְּעָלְמָא דְּאָתֵי מַמָּשׁ
and they have not merited to be truly in the World to Come
that death will be for him merely like sleep,
וְאַחַר כָּךְ הָקִיצוּ וְרַנְּנוּ (יְשַׁעְיָה כו, יט)
"'When you lie down, it shall guard over you' — this is death;
'and when you awaken, it shall converse with you' — in the time to come,"
so that it will be merely like waking from sleep
וְיוּכַל כָּל אֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל לִזְכּוֹת לָזֶה
And every one of Yisrael can merit this
עַל יְדֵי שֶׁשּׁוֹנֶה הֲלָכוֹת בְּכָל יוֹם:
"Whoever expands upon the telling of Yetzias Mitzrayim
This implies that one must innovate
something on the subject of Yetzias Mitzrayim;
of the story itself we know nothing
but what is written in the Torah
and received from our Sages, of blessed memory.
And we do not find that they instituted
the recital of all the accounts,
even for the choicest fulfillment of the mitzvah
and for the most meticulous of the meticulous.
So perforce, indeed, the "one who expands" who is praiseworthy
means that it should include innovating
and adding, on the subject of the telling,
from his own mind, some praises to the Omnipresent
of the good that He did for us
beyond what is told and known.
And likewise, the episode in which they told the story all night
what they innovated in expounding on this,
And since nothing of their telling is found
in the Midrashim, the Mechilta and the like,
in the words of our Sages, of blessed memory,
נִרְאֶה דִּלְפִי שֶׁלֹּא הָיוּ תַּלְמִידֵיהֶם עִמָּהֶם,
it appears that since their students were not with them,
it appears that they were occupied with secrets and hidden matters
which are not to be revealed to students,
וְעַל כֵּן לֹא נִתְגַּלּוּ דִּבְרֵיהֶם לָנוּ.
and therefore their words were not revealed to us.
And it appears that what they said,
for then everyone has license to expand;
as is known from the sefarim,
Pesach alludes to "peh sach" — the mouth speaks;
for previously speech was in exile,
דְּעַל כֵּן אָמַר מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
which is why Moshe Rabbeinu, alav hashalom, said,
לֹא אִישׁ דְּבָרִים אָנֹכִי (שְׁמוֹת ד, י).
"I am not a man of words" (Shemos 4:10).
which is the exodus of speech from exile,
which is awakened every year at that time,
as is known regarding the holiness of the set times,
can multiply words as he wishes.
"And they shall turn back and encamp before Pi HaChiros"
that one must settle his mind and encamp
before he lets his mouth out to freedom,
to speak whatever comes to his mind.
וּפָסוּק זֶה נֶאֱמַר בְּיוֹם שְׁלִישִׁי דְּפֶסַח,
And this pasuk was said on the third day of Pesach,
when they turned back toward Mitzrayim
that was present on the first two days —
for the second day in chutz la'aretz, too,
יֵשׁ בּוֹ אוֹתוֹ הָאוֹר דְּיוֹם רִאשׁוֹן,
has in it the same light as the first day,
וְגַם הֵם הָיוּ אָז בְּחוּץ לָאָרֶץ;
and they too were then in chutz la'aretz;
and even though they sanctified the month there
and knew when Rosh Chodesh was,
on Yom Tov Sheni shel Galuyos
Therefore, on the first two days,
the mouth speaks in freedom as it wishes,
and only on the third day is it alluded
that one still needs to settle his mind a great deal
for it is not yet complete freedom.
